newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil minister seeks funds for refineries.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil minister seeks funds for refineries.

text.p: Nigerian oil minister Dan Etete has urged the military government to release funds to repair the nation's four oil refineries, his aides said on Tuesday.
The low productivity of the refineries is partly to blame for a three-week-old fuel supply crunch that has caused long queues of vehicles at pump stations.

His aides said Etete, addressing the committee on Vision 2010 in the capital Abuja last week, lamented that four months into 1997 the government was yet to release $230 million voted for the oil sector to refurbish the refineries and pipelines.
Vision 2010 committee is a 197-strong group of business and political leaders appointed by the military government to fashion ways of improving Nigeria's economy.
Etete said practical measures were needed to strengthen the oil industry, Nigeria's economic backbone.
The sector is heavily underfunded despite providing the bulk of Nigeria's export revenue.

Poor management and inadequate maintenance are responsible for why the four refineries often run at a fraction of their combined installed capacity to process 445,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil.
Etete said Nigeria's oil industry was beset with a series of problems including ageing refineries, vandalised pipelines and poor maintenance of fuel depots and pump stations.
"In general, the refineries, except for the new Port Harcourt plant, are old and often face equipment failure and breakdowns," he said, adding "They require a comprehesive rehabilitation programme."
A turn around maintenance of the plants due to have been undertaken in the first quarter of this year was reschuled to late summer after the finance ministry failed to release funding on schedule.
